name: Agent Memory and Planning
blurb: How agents remember, plan, and recover.

repos.name: mem0
repos.description: The Memory Layer for AI Agents - Drop-in memory infrastructure for AI agents and apps. Context that persists. Built for production.

repos.name: letta
repos.description: Platform for stateful agents: AI with advanced memory that can learn and self-improve over time.

reading.body:
Agent memory infrastructure is the narrowest part of the three-repository open source ecosystem for persistent agent memory, with mem0 commanding 69 percent of aggregate GitHub stars while the two alternatives remain substantially smaller.

The concentration of development attention on mem0 reflects a market ordering around production readiness. All three projects target the same problem: agents that can retain and learn from context across interactions rather than starting fresh each session. mem0 frames this explicitly as infrastructure, letta as a platform for self-improvement, and zep more minimally. The gap in stars suggests the market is consolidating around one approach.

This matters for AI deployment because agent memory is not a solved problem at scale. Current LLMs have fixed context windows and no persistent learning. Memory systems sit between the model and the application, absorbing the compute cost of retrieval and the storage cost of history. As agents handle longer-running tasks, memory becomes a scaling bottleneck. The consolidation here indicates which infrastructure layer may see the heaviest investment and refinement.

The data covers only open source repositories and does not capture proprietary systems or commercial adoption. It reflects developer interest on GitHub rather than production usage or economic value. It does not show whether these tools actually reduce the compute required for agents to function, or whether they primarily redistribute it.
